concept.title: Choose between CIS levels, channels, and generated layers
concept.shortdesc: CIS selection in BPM depends on the intended hardening level and the Firefox schema channel used for validation and export.

section.title: Level 1
section.p: Level 1 is the default starting point for broad enterprise use. In BPM it is represented by generated Level 1 layers for ESR 115.38, ESR 140.13, ESR 153.0, and Release 153, each covering 49 mapped recommendations. Use it when the profile should improve security posture while preserving routine browsing and support workflows.

section.title: Level 2
section.p: Level 2 is stricter and adds controls that may affect usability, operations, or troubleshooting. BPM generates Level 2 layers for ESR 115.38, ESR 140.13, ESR 153.0, and Release 153, each covering 53 mapped recommendations. Choose it only when the deployment owner accepts stronger restrictions and has a review process for exceptions.

section.title: Supported Firefox channels
section.p: BPM supports Firefox ESR 115.38, ESR 140.13, ESR 153.0, and Release 153 schemas. Generated CIS layers are available for every one of these exact artifacts. Keep the selected schema channel consistent until export and use the matching generated layer; availability is schema validation evidence, not CIS certification or endorsement.

section.title: Generated layers
section.p: The available generated layers are cis-l1.esr-115.38, cis-l1.esr-140.13, cis-l1.esr-153.0, cis-l1.release-153, cis-l2.esr-115.38, cis-l2.esr-140.13, cis-l2.esr-153.0, and cis-l2.release-153. Each layer contributes BPM-owned policy values or locked managed preferences, then the profile merge logic records whether a value was added, already satisfied, replaced, stricter in the base, or kept for manual review.

section.title: Manual review
section.p: Nine explicit paths require manual review because local governance can change the correct decision. Update controls, proxy mode and lock state, and selected sanitize-on-shutdown values are examples where BPM surfaces the issue but does not make a universal compliance decision.
